title: Public async job lifecycle: status, paginated results, per-URL errors, cancel/pause/resume, origin and live tail
summary: Expose the missing job lifecycle for crawl and batch: GET /v1/crawl/:id (status, completed/total, warnings, expiry, cursor-paged data capped at 100 docs or 10 MiB), GET /v1/crawl/:id/errors (per-URL failures including robots-blocked), GET /v1/crawl/ongoing, DELETE /v1/crawl/:id (cancel) and POST pause/resume, with /v1/batch aliases. Turn /v1/jobs/:id/events into a real live tail that sends a catch-up snapshot first and supports Last-Event-ID. || Add authenticated, org-checked routes on the Quarry edge and the gateway for crawl status, cancel, pause and resume that map onto the Temporal signals the crawl workflow already handles. Add a live SSE tail for job events, a recorded run origin (user, agent, schedule, webhook, api) and a stage timeline on the job record, and surface the controls in the crawl UI and as Model Plane tools.
whyItMatters: Users notice immediately when a runaway crawl cannot be stopped or a failed page cannot be explained, and agents need a single poll call. This is also the dependency for webhooks, waiters, resumable timeouts and monitors. The Temporal cancel/pause/resume handlers already exist, so most of the work is route wiring rather than new engine logic. || A user or agent who starts a crawl today (up to 5000 pages) has no way to stop, pause or inspect it from the product. Agents need the same controls to honour budgets, and the audit model needs to know who or what started a run.

others: Apify (run lifecycle contract with graceful abort, resurrect, origin)

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: GET /crawl/:id returns {status, completed, total, creditsUsed, expiresAt, data[page], next, warnings[]} where the page ends at 100 docs or 10 MiB and the cursor advances by what was actually returned; /errors returns [{url, code, error, requiresAction}] plus robotsBlocked[]; DELETE sends a cancel signal; results expire by TTL. The stream sends {type:'catchup', data: status}, then each finished document, then done, with defined close codes; support Last-Event-ID so reconnects do not lose events (the reference polls once a second server-side and its SDK falls back to polling, so build the tail off durable event history instead). || Merged items add: A state machine is persisted on the run record with a timestamp per transition and an origin. Abort emits an aborting event, waits a grace period (30 s on Apify) and then hard-stops. State is persisted periodically and on a migrating event so a run can resume. Resurrect restarts the timer with the same storage ids. Firecrawl records an array of steps so a UI can draw a timeline.

title: Make scrape, crawl and batch schedules actually execute (Temporal schedules)
summary: Map crawl, scrape and batch schedule target kinds to Temporal ScheduleSpec instead of skipping them, wire a Temporal client into quarry-control so trigger and backfill stop returning 501, add a timezone field and record skipped reasons as job events. Until this ships, stop the gateway UI offering actions the backend cannot perform.
whyItMatters: Scheduled re-crawls of tracked sources keep Verevon's knowledge fresh, and the UI already lets users create such schedules. Today only change_monitor schedules run, so users can create schedules that silently never fire, which erodes trust and leaves knowledge stale.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (scheduler with lease claim, deterministic jitter, skipped_overlap/skipped_no_credits, stale recovery, plain-English cron)
others: Apify (timezone-aware cron, per-run input overrides, failure notifications)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Scheduler tick selects due schedules FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and sets lease_until; fire_at = next_cron(tz) + sha256(id) mod min(interval/2, 5 min); if the previous run is still active record skipped_overlap and advance; if entitlement is insufficient record skipped_no_credits; otherwise reserve credits, start the workflow with the stored input override and advance next_run_at. Runs active past a threshold are marked failed and released. A phrase parser turns 'every 30 minutes' into cron with a 5-minute minimum. Failures notify the owner.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: workflowFor in schedule_wire.go maps only change_monitor to a workflow; scrape, crawl and batch return an empty workflow and the orchestrator skips them (the code comment says they are not run_id-safe for recurring dispatch yet). MountScheduleAliases receives a nil Temporal client, so trigger and backfill return a typed 501. Cron is a strict 5-field expression with no timezone, and there is no jitter or skipped-reason status. The gateway UI exposes overlap policy, pause, trigger and backfill that the backend cannot fully honour (INF from comparing gateway and control code).

approachOriginal: Ingestion Plane. Extend workflowFor to return CrawlJobWF, scrape and batch workflow names plus args, deriving a fresh replay-safe run_id from each scheduled workflow execution exactly as ChangeMonitorWF already does. Let Temporal schedules provide overlap policy (skip), jitter, timezone and backfill rather than building a custom Firecrawl-style scheduler. Inject the Temporal client into quarry-control (MountScheduleAliases) so trigger and backfill work. Add a timezone column and spec field, write skipped/failed reasons as job events, and send failure notifications via notification-core in the Application Plane. Scheduled fires must inherit the org's ZDR floor and re-check entitlement at fire time, not only at create time. Migrate with an explicit enable step so previously created schedules do not all start firing at once.
dependencies: Temporal client in quarry-control
F-t2-008 entitlement check for a skipped_no_credits state
notification-core for failure notices
risks: Existing schedules will start firing after the fix, which can surprise users and spend budget; require an explicit re-enable. Recurring crawls without R-t2-05-01 scoping would repeat the off-site walk, so sequence after scoping.

title: Structured extraction that works in production: json, summary, question and highlights formats over a real Model Plane structured-output grant
summary: Add json (schema plus prompt, strict-schema normalisation, JSON repair), summary, question and highlights as ScrapeOptions formats on scrape and crawl, executed by calling a Model Plane structured-output endpoint over an org-bound, metered model-invoke grant. Today the prompt field is dead code, JSON exists only on /v1/extract, and the cross-plane token manifest denies model-invoke, so extraction only works under dev bypass (SRC). The grant is a tracked deferral (DEF-QB-T17-PART2, owner and date unassigned).
whyItMatters: Schema-to-JSON extraction is the most-used LLM feature of scrape APIs and the basis for monitors, research jobs and extraction profiles. The Model Plane already centralises ZDR-aware model routing, so Quarry should call it rather than hold its own model keys.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (engine-and-infra-090 and api-surface-042 for json; api-surface-046 for summary/question/highlights)
others: Firecrawl (api-surface fc-023: /extract deprecated in favour of a json format on /scrape plus the agent)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources in this record set (Firecrawl); common among scrape platforms (INF: LLM extraction is widely offered; Apify has no record for it in this set) for json, unique for question/highlights || structured LLM extraction as a built-in API: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl), differentiator for scraping APIs
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: normalizeSchema (additionalProperties:false, every field required, $ref resolved) then validate for strict mode with clear errors; pick the model by schema complexity ($ref/$defs go to a larger model); trim markdown by character bound then tokenizer to 80 percent of the context; call with response_format json_schema strict; on parse failure run a repair pass; on provider error fall back to the next provider; return data + warnings + token usage. summary, question and highlights are each one LLM call over trimmed markdown (10,000-char inputs) with a fixed instruction, returned as document.summary|answer|highlights; billed per page. || Merged items add: formats:[{type:'json', schema, prompt}] on scrape: convert the page to markdown, call the LLM with schema-constrained output, validate against the schema, return data.json; multi-page work goes through batch or the agent; the old /extract stays with Deprecation headers pointing to the new shape.

title: Harden persistent browser profiles: complete snapshots, per-org envelope encryption at rest, ordered saves, ZDR enforced inside Quarry
summary: Capture cookie expiry, storage for every origin and IndexedDB in profile snapshots; envelope-encrypt snapshots (and secret job inputs) per org and owner with keys obtained through a Control Plane key API (env master key first, KMS later); add monotonic saved_at and deletion tombstones; wire the S3 store and the GDPR purge consumer; and enforce in Quarry, not only in the UI, that ZDR orgs get no persistent profile.
whyItMatters: Persistent profiles hold live session cookies for users' signed-in sites. Today snapshots are incomplete and not encrypted at rest (SRC), which is a data-governance risk that grows with every login handed to the agent. Encryption is specified in docs/CONTRACTS.md:185-199 but not implemented.

others: Apify SessionPool with session-to-proxy-IP pinning (apify-platform-059, DOC)
Firecrawl: caller cookies seeded through the browser cookie jar, not a header (firecrawl-engine-and-infra-010, SRC)
Apify (secret inputs encrypted per user and Actor, decrypted only inside the run)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 4 sources (apify, firecrawl), table-stakes || 1 of 4 sources; unique (adopted here as a security baseline, not a feature)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Profile = {id, scope, owner, fingerprint, egress affinity, snapshot blob ref, saved_at, deleted_at}. Save is an UPSERT with saved_at = GREATEST(saved_at, new) and is ignored when a newer deletion tombstone exists, so a late save cannot resurrect a deleted profile. Snapshot = all cookies (expiry, SameSite, partition key) + local/session storage per origin + IndexedDB export, encrypted with a per-org key. Profiles are refused under ZDR, lockdown and Safe Mode. Caller cookies go in with Network.setCookies at the registrable domain. || Merged items add: On save generate a random AES-256-GCM key, encrypt the value, wrap that key with an RSA-2048 public key unique to (user, tool) and persist ENCRYPTED_VALUE:<wrapped>:<ciphertext>. At run start the runtime receives the private key through a mounted file or env and decrypts in process; logs and stored input keep only ciphertext.

title: Org-pinned, tighten-only web policy: tri-state capability gates delivered as signed claims and enforced by Quarry
summary: Make the Control Plane the policy of record for web and browser capabilities (robots mode and override, maximum proxy tier, credential/cookie/header stripping, login or form-write actions for autonomous runs, raw evaluate, uploads and downloads, recording, persistent profiles, paid providers, domain allow/deny, ZDR) as disabled/allowed/forced, delivered on the signed-claim channel that already carries the ZDR floor and inside BrowserBroker grants as action classes. Quarry rejects at the edge and re-resolves per URL in PageRunner and the step path as a backstop. Requests, Spaces and the Model can only tighten.
whyItMatters: This is the direct implementation of three Verevon rules: Quarry executes or rejects, ZDR must propagate, and Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL. Today two RunPolicy types exist and the edge hard-wires RunPolicy::default(), so no org or request policy is applied (SRC); control-plane presets are not consumed. Firecrawl Safe Mode (SRC) is the reference shape.

others: Firecrawl (per-team tri-state flags and per-key restrictions), with Codex's default-off browser gates
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl); unique, but it maps onto Verevon's own governance rules || 2 of 4 sources; differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: ResolvedPolicy = merge(orgPolicy, defaults) is computed in the API layer, which rejects requests that ask for forbidden options (403 SAFE_MODE_BLOCKED), and is recomputed in the worker for every URL including crawl children as a backstop that downgrades instead of trusting the request. It strips Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization, write/press/executeJavascript actions, profiles and URL userinfo, blocks browser endpoints, and bypasses allow-listed domains. All violations produce audit events. || Merged items add: Firecrawl TeamFlags hold disabled|allowed|forced per capability (ZDR for scrape and search can be forced, plus ignoreRobots, threatProtection, ipWhitelist); effective option = forced ? on : (allowed ? request : reject with typed error). Keys additionally carry allowedEndpoints and allowedFormats, checked per request and cached about 60 s. Codex keeps fine-grained gates (browserUse, full CDP access, webMcp, record-and-replay, auto-auth-for-sites, multi-window) that default to off with a dev-only env override.

Enforce at the edge by rejecting with a typed sub-code, and again in PageRunner and agent step execution per URL (including crawl children and redirects), downgrading rather than trusting the request. CONFLICT: the claim channel that carries the ZDR floor only reaches user-token callers (gateway UI paths). execution-core and model-gateway call Quarry with service tokens whose zdr claim is true for every org and is deliberately ignored, so for Model-Plane-driven runs the resolved policy has to ride in the BrowserBroker grant or the start-run body set by the Model Plane. verevon.approachAdjustment: Run the ADR first: org-core claims versus capability-core grants (capability-core already has tenant-bound org-scope grants and a single coarse browser capability). verevon.verdictReason: Direction is right and nothing substantial exists, but the delivery channel is wrong for the agent path, capability-core grants already exist as a competing policy of record, and a Quarry-only first slice is missing from the plan.

reference.corrections: Firecrawl action execution happens only in the closed hosted fire-engine (chrome-cdp); the open-source playwright engine declares actions:false, so 'execute sequentially on one page' is not observable in source and self-hosted Firecrawl cannot run actions. Outputs are grouped into per-type arrays (screenshots, scrapes, javascriptReturns, pdfs), not one ordered per-action results array (an ordered array is a Verevon improvement, mark INF). The scrape executeJavascript action has no script-size cap; the 100,000-byte / 1-300 s limits belong to the separate hosted-browser /execute endpoint (Hangar), so do not attribute a script cap to the scrape action DSL. Aside always scroll-stitches with captureBeyondViewport:false (single tile when content fits the viewport); the 'captureBeyondViewport when within limit' branch is Codex/Firecrawl-style, so the merged mechanism blends sources and should say so. JPEG q80 and fresh-frame screencast are Codex-specific; Aside tiles are PNG and element shots default to webp.

title: Credential handoff where the model never sees secrets: executor-side fill_secret and email OTP via integration-corev2
summary: Add a fill_secret action carrying an opaque vault:// reference that Quarry resolves only at execution time through the integration-corev2 token broker, fills in an isolated world after re-checking origin and field type, and then blocks page observation of the filled value; add an IC mail.otp.read action so email one-time codes are delivered by the executor after user approval. Requires a sensitive BrowserBroker grant, capture-time redaction (F-t2-021), trusted input (F-t2-015), takeover (F-t2-013) and a Model Plane elicitation/approval card.
whyItMatters: Both browser references keep secrets out of the model (Codex: isolated-world fill, OTP and QR, SRC; Aside: origin-bound vault refs, SRC). Verevon has no secret references; fill_secret exists only as a plan (reconciled plan section 19.1, DOC). The present fallback, human takeover login into a scoped profile, works for attended runs but blocks unattended agents and routines.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Agent calls request({origin, fields[{label, selector, autocomplete}], submit}). The runtime validates origin and selector uniqueness/visibility; the UI shows a secure form or vault picker; values travel executor -> CDP isolated world -> input.value plus input events; the agent receives only {status}. The document is marked credential-delivered and AX/DOM/screenshot reads of that loader id are denied until navigation. || Merged items add: Model calls browserAuth.request(otpHandle) on a tab. Runtime proceeds only if: origin is https; frame origin equals top origin; exactly one required non-password input; no options/QR; credential-observation gate on; conversation id bound; otherwise status 'unavailable'. It then raises a user elicitation (kind browser_email_otp, requires user input, not auto-approvable by a guardian) saying the model cannot see the code and the user may type it instead. On approval the host (not the model runtime) fetches the code from the mail connector over a local broker socket (versioned credential binding) and types it through a native input path; the model receives only a status. Note Codex restricts this to non-password fields.

approachOriginal: ADR on secret custody across planes first (IC owns secrets; Quarry resolves at execution; Model Plane sees only the reference). Then IC operations, Quarry fill_secret with origin and field preconditions plus redaction, Model Plane elicitation event and frontend approval card. || Source detail: [R-t2-09-04] Ingestion Plane: fill_secret action plus an observation gate and redaction of receipts and live frames (blank or blur credential fields). Frontend: secure credential form outside the live frame. Secret store with opaque references scoped to user/org lives in the owning plane (Control Plane per the comparator; check integration-corev2 credential handling first) and is read through its API only. Model Plane: planner sees only ref ids and status. || [R-t2-10-01] Ingestion Plane owns execution; Model Plane owns the approval. (1) Quarry contracts (quarry-core contracts.rs AgentAction plus the Go pkg/quarrycontracts mirror): add FillSecretRef { snapshot_id, generation, ref_id, secret_ref } and FillOtpRef; secret_ref is an opaque handle such as secret://connection/<id>/mail-otp, never a value. (2) browser-broker: add a fill_secret entry to allowedSensitiveActions and issue it through CreateScopedSensitiveApproval as a single-use child of the run grant, bound to one origin, one frame and one secret_ref with a short TTL, only after a user approval event routed by Model Plane/Conversation. (3) integration-corev2: add a dedicated mail.otp.read action (sender/age/pattern filters, returns the code only, write-attested user context, audited through the existing outbox) so Quarry never holds a mailbox OAuth token; do not just add quarry to INTEGRATION_TOKEN_LEASE_CONSUMERS. Add the Quarry-to-IC row to the cross-plane service-token manifest. (4) Quarry executor: precondition checks (https, frame origin == top origin == grant origin, exactly one visible required non-password input for OTP, no QR/options), fill via CDP Input.insertText, mask the field in screenshots/DOM snapshots, receipts carry a boolean only, nothing persisted under ZDR. (5) Frontend: elicitation card naming origin and connection, stating the model cannot see the value, and offering "I will type it myself". Ship OTP first; passwords/vault secrets only after the redaction and prompt-injection defences are proven.

verevon.constraints: Ingestion Plane owns execution and secret resolution, and the model only ever sees opaque references (Model proposes, Quarry executes); secrets are scoped to user or org and never widened by Space access. ZDR: no persistence of values or frames showing credentials, yet non-ZDR receipts today store typed text verbatim, so redaction (F-t2-021) must precede any fill action. IC Vault is token-at-rest encryption, not a user-secret store, so a secret-custody ADR is required before password references; IC internal auth is one shared API key (server.go:170-173), so Quarry to IC needs a distinct identity or manifest row, and the OTP action must stay off any Model-callable tool surface and return only the code. Production BrowserBroker grant issuance is unbuilt (shared prerequisite with F-t2-001 and F-t2-013).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Ship OTP first: add a fill_otp variant beside upload_ref and download_ref in the existing sensitive-approval path (single-use child grant bound to run grant, frame and origin), an executor-only IC mail.otp.read action, and reuse the Login risk gate and orchestration approvals for the approval card instead of a new elicitation channel. Defer password and vault-secret references until the secret-custody ADR, F-t2-021 redaction and F-t2-015 trusted input are in place. Do not add quarry to INTEGRATION_TOKEN_LEASE_CONSUMERS.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for the OTP-first slice; the full password and secret-store scope would be XL because of the ADR, redaction and grant-issuance prerequisites.
